new_entities.name: Cancer detection rate

new_entities.description: The rate at which screening identifies breast cancers in an eligible population.

edges.effect_quant: In dense-breast screening populations, supplemental MRI consistently adds materially more cancer detections than mammography alone, with meta-analytic estimates around 19 additional cancers per 1000 screenings and DENSE trial MRI detection around 16.5 per 1000 screenings.
edges.population: women with dense or extremely dense breast tissue undergoing screening mammography, especially average- or intermediate-risk dense-breast cohorts
edges.mechanism: MRI is much less limited by dense fibroglandular tissue than mammography, allowing it to reveal biologically relevant lesions that are masked on standard breast X-ray screening.
edges.summary: Supplemental MRI in dense breasts is one of the strongest yield-improvement strategies in breast screening. The evidence is more persuasive for improved detection and fewer interval cancers than for broad population implementation, but the direction on detection rate is clearly protective.
edges.caveats: Higher detection comes with more recalls, more biopsies, and greater cost and access burden. This edge focuses on cancer detection yield, not on overdiagnosis, net harm, or policy-level cost-effectiveness.
